A Bench of Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana observed the portal had already been opened for all candidates for a specified period and that reopening it could trigger lakhs of fresh claims. The plea pointed out that OSM was implemented for the first time in 2026 and that teachers were not provided formal training before its implementation. items.title: Allahabad High Court takes serious note of IAS officer's alleged attempt to influence trial judge
items.summary: The Allahabad High Court recently expressed concern over allegations that senior Indian Administrative Service (IAS) officer Durga Shakti Nagpal had attempted to pressure a trial judge through a phone call in connection with a long-pending land case [ Jyoti Vidya Mandir v Nagar Palika Parishad & Ors. ]. In a letter to the district judge, the civil judge alleged that the IAS officer attempted to exert pressure on her during a phone conversation by questioning her about her leave and seeking to discuss a pending case. The IAS officer has maintained that she had not tried to discuss the merits of the case, and had only sought to know when the judge would resume hearing the matter. On August 21, Justice Syed Qamar Hasan Rizvi of the High Court took a serious view of the allegations against the IAS officer. "The tone and language of the aforesaid alleged telephonic conversation given a direct impression that the Presiding Officer of the Court was tried to be influenced and that made her feel offended ... It is shocking that how a litigating party can approach the Court by making such a phone call and that too in context with a pending matter before the said Court ," observed the Court.

Reddy said the additional annual charge would come at a time when households were already dealing with rising living costs and financial commitments such as education, healthcare, vehicle loans and other expenses. items.title: Better-half will become bitter-half if issues not addressed: Delhi HC acquits man for murder attempt against wife
items.summary: Marriage is paradoxical and a world of extremities, the Delhi High Court recently observed while acquitting a man who was convicted by a trial court for attempting to murder his wife by forcing Baygon Spray (an insecticide) down her throat [Nafe Singh v State] . Justice Vimal Kumar Yadav said that “the best, in no time, becomes worst if not handled carefully”. The Court highlighted recent examples wherein spouses resorted to extreme levels of violence against each other, which was incomprehensible some decades ago. “The better-half becomes the bitter-half if issues are not taken care of and resolved as soon as possible. One of the most beautiful relationships of humans, that is of a husband and wife becomes one of the most terrible when things go wrong in a matrimonial alliance. Time, albeit, is a big healer and tones down a lot of pains in life, however in relationships time taken can also be counterproductive,” the Court stressed. It added that relationships can go in a totally different, undesirable, and unexpected direction if not handled carefully. items.title: Forensic evidence should aid cases, not create more burden for survivors: Ex-ASG Pinky Anand
items.summary: Better forensic practices should strengthen cases before courts without creating an additional burden of proof for survivors of sexual and gender-based violence, former Additional Solicitor General of India Pinky Anand said at a training workshop in Goa on Saturday. The day-long workshop, held on August 22, focused on implementing Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) for the collection, preservation, chain of custody and presentation of forensic evidence in cases of sexual assault, rape and child abuse. “Better forensic practice must strengthen the case that reaches the court. It must never become a fresh threshold of belief that survivors are asked to clear,” said Anand. The SOPs were formally launched by Anand at the Police Headquarters in Panjim on April 26 last year, marking World DNA Day. They were subsequently expanded to include the handling of forensic evidence in cases involving child abuse. items.title: Karnataka High Court stays proceedings against man accused of ghosting, seen-zoning his partner
items.summary: The Karnataka High Court recently stayed criminal proceedings against a man accused of sex on the false promise of marriage after ghosting and 'seen-zoning' his partner [Thufail Ahmed v. State] . Justice M Nagaprasanna observed that the petitioner's conduct did not fulfil the ingredients of Section 69 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023. "It is the allegation that the petitioner had begun to seenzone the respondent and ghost her throughout. Therefore, the offence under s.69 has sprung. Except this there is nothing else that could become the ingredients of the offence under s.69. In that light there shall be an interim order of stay on further proceedings qua the petitioner till the next date of hearing." Justice M Nagaprasanna Both parties were in a relationship since December 2025. The petitioner told his then partner that he was visiting Chennai, where ailing father was undergoing treatment. The ex-partner, suspecting that the petitioner had told her a lie, asked him to receive her video call. The petitioner refused to receive calls and eventually blocked her. The woman then filed a complaint alleging that the petitioner had committed offences of Section 69 and 115, BNS .

items.title: Supreme Court bans construction activities within 100 meters of Rajasthan's Jojari River
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Monday banned all construction and development activities within 100 metres from the edge of Rajasthan's Jojari River till the conclusion of scientific determination and demarcation of the high flood line and ecological buffer zones [ In Re: 2 Million Lives At Risk, Contamination In Jojari River, Rajasthan ]. A Bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta passed the order in a suo motu case concerning industrial pollution of rivers in Rajasthan, including the Jojari River. " We are of the considered view that it is necessary to put in place an interim, definite and measurable area of protection so as to adequately safeguard the riverine ecosystem during the pendency of the scientific exercise for the determination and demarcation of the high flood line and the requisite ecological buffer zones. Hence, we hereby direct that no construction or development activity of any nature whatsoever shall be permitted within a distance of 100 meters from the edge of the river in accordance with the aforesaid guidelines," the Court ordered. items.title: Datura sold as food online: Karnataka suspends Amazon, Swiggy, BigBasket licences
items.summary: Follow TNM's WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. The Karnataka Food Safety and Drug Administration Department has suspended the food licences of Amazon, Swiggy Instamart and BigBasket until further orders after toxic Datura fruits and seeds were found being sold online as food products. According to an order issued by Food Safety Commissioner K Srinivas, the department has also directed the three platforms to immediately remove listings and advertisements for Datura, also known as Dhatura, and stop selling or distributing the products for human consumption. Datura, known as jimsonweed or devil’s trumpet, is a highly poisonous plant. It is traditionally used in religious rituals, ornamental gardening and some Ayurvedic practices. The entire plant, including its fruits and seeds, is toxic and can cause severe poisoning and death if consumed. Extremely diluted mixtures of the plant are used in Ayurvedic medicines for various purposes.
